questions.question: The chemical formula of Iron (III) oxide is _________.
questions.solution:

• The chemical formula of Iron (III) oxide is **Fe₂O₃ __**

questions.question: The sum of the first 2007 terms of the sequence 1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2, 3, 4, _______ is:
questions.solution:
Here, we have repeated series of the first 4 terms i.e. 1,2,3,4 and the sum becomes 10

⇒ Total number of such repeated series = 2004/4 = 501

⇒ Sum of the first 2004 terms = 501 × 10 = 5010

∴ Sum of the first 2007 terms = 5010 + 1 + 2 + 3 = 5016

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/52518c955aa39d19db8c33df7ef37b06d52cf2832e484eed918cce85751c22c1.png] 

In this question, We have to find the sum of 1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2, 3, 4... at 2007-terms. At 2004-terms all four terms (1, 2, 3 and 4) repeat continuously but after 2004 only 1, 2, and 3 occurs for completing 2007 terms. therefore first we have to find the sum of 2004 terms and after we added sum of 1, 2 and 3 in the sum of 2004 terms.

questions.question: Rs. 1,125 invested for 3 months gave an interest of Rs. 27. What was the simple rate of interest per annum?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal = Rs 1125

Time = 3 months = 1/4 year = 0.25 year

Interest = Rs 27

**Concept used:**

Simple Interest = (Principal × rate of interest × time)/100

**Calculation:**

Time in years = 3/12

⇒ 27 = (1125 × R × 0.25)/1200

⇒ R = 9.6%

**∴ The rate of interest was 9.6% per annum**

questions.question: A mobile when sold at a gain of 6% yields Rs. 870 more than when it is sold at a loss of 6%. What is the cost price of the mobile phone?
questions.solution:
Let the cost price of phone be x.

According to the question

1.06x – 0.94x = Rs. 870

⇒ 0.12x = 870

⇒ x = Rs. 7250

∴ The cost price of phone is Rs. 7250

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** **Given:**

SP at 6% profit is Rs. 870 more than SP at 6% loss.

**Formula used:**

SP = CP × (100 + P%)/100

Also, SP = CP × (100 - L%)/100

**Calculation:**

Let CP be 100

When profit is 6%,

⇒ SP = 100 × (100 + 6)/100 = 106

Similarly, when loss is 6%

⇒ SP = 94

According to the question,

⇒ 106 - 94 = 870

⇒ 12 units = 870

⇒ 1 unit = 72.5

⇒ 100 units = 7250

**∴ The required CP is Rs. 7250.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__** (Profit%) + (Loss%) = Difference in SP's

⇒ 6% + 6% = 870

⇒ 12% = 870

⇒ 100% = 7250

**∴ The required CP is Rs. 7250.**

questions.question: If an electric iron rated 1000W is operated for 3 hours/day, final the total energy consumed in 30 days in Kwh.
questions.solution:
Given data

⇒ Rated value of the electric lamp (P) = 1000 watts

⇒ Amount of time the iron is being used = 3 × 30 = 90 hours

⇒ t = 90 h

We know that, Power(P) = E/t

Where ‘P’ is power in watts and ‘E’ is energy consumed in watt-hours and ‘t’ is time.

Substituting the values in the above equation, we get

1000 = E/90

E = 90000 Watt-Hours

E = 90 kWh or units. (1 Kilo Watt Hour = 1 unit)

Hence, the energy consumed by the lamp in 30 days (E) = **__90 kWh__**

questions.question: Frictional force acts __________.

options.text: Against the direction of the force
At any angle to the direction of the force
In the direction of the force
Perpendicular to the direction of the force

questions.solution:
__
 
• The force of friction always acts in a direction opposite to that in which the body tends to move, means** against the direction of the force.__**
 
• Till the limiting value is reached, the magnitude of friction is exactly equal to the force which tends to move the body.
 
• The magnitude of the limiting friction bears a constant ratio to the normal reaction between the two surfaces.
 
• The force of friction depends upon the roughness/smoothness of the surfaces.
 
• The force of friction is independent of the area of contact between the two surfaces.

questions.question:
Can you tell which argument is strong?

**Statement:**

Should government take priority in linking rivers?

**Arguments:**

I. Yes, in the long run this will entirely eradicate water shortages in remote areas.

II. No, we shouldn’t contaminate water and the rivers will naturally take its course.

options.text: Both I and II are strong
Neither I nor II is strong.

questions.solution:
• The statement is talking about linking the rivers. The argument I claims that linking the rivers will lead to complete “eradication of water shortage in remote areas”. Taking steps that can eradicate water shortage, in the long run, is necessary and a must. Therefore, this can be considered a strong reason to prioritize linking rivers. Hence, argument I is strong.
 
• Argument II is talking about “river contamination” which is not mentioned in the statement at all.
 
• Hence, only argument I is strong.

questions.question: The mass number of an isotope of an element is 298. If its nucleus has 189 neutrons, what is its atomic number?
questions.solution:
__
 
• The** Mass number** is always equal to the sum of the number of protons and the number of neutrons. The mass number determines the Atomic mass of an atom, Mass Number is denoted by A
 
• The **Atomic number** of an element is the number of protons present in the nucleus of an atom, Atomic Number is denoted by Z.

Atomic Number = Number of Protons

Mass Number = Number of Protons + Number of Neutrons

 
• Here, Mass Number = 298

Number of Protons + Number of Neutrons = 298

Number of Protons = 298 - 189 = 109

Hence, Atomic Number = **109 __**[As, Atomic Number = Number of Protons]

 
• **Isotopes **are defined as elements with the same number of protons but a different number of neutrons present in their nucleus. As the electrons remain the same, so their chemical properties don’t change however due to change in neutron number their atomic mass is changed which results in different physical properties like melting, colour, etc.

questions.question: Three flood gates A, B and C can fill a reservoir in 6 hours. After working at it together for 2 hours, flood gate C is closed. Flood gates A and B can fill the remaining part in 7 hours. The number of hours taken by flood gate C alone to fill the reservoir is:
questions.solution:
Reservoir filled in 1 hour by flood gates A, B and C together = 1/6

⇒ Reservoir filled in 2 hours by all gates = 1/3

⇒ Reservoir left to be filled = 1 – 1/3 = 2/3

⇒ Reservoir filled in 1 hour by flood gates A and B = 2/21

⇒ Reservoir filled in 1 hour by gate C = 1/6 – 2/21 = 3/42

∴ Flood gate C alone filled the reservoir in 14 hours.

K.E = p²/2 m

→ now momentum remains the same as said above

Therefore, K.E ∝ 1/2 m

K.E is inversely proportional to the mass of the body

 
• Therefore body having less mass will have greater kinetic energy and vice versa
 
• Here, in this case, the bullet is lighter than the gun, therefore, the kinetic energy of the bullet is more than that of the gun.

questions.question: A truck falls off a ledge and drops to the ground in 0.8 secs. How high is the ledge from the ground? (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.solution:
Using the second law of motion to compute the height of the ledge

s = ut + ½ gt² 

s = height of the ledge

u = Initial velocity

t = time

g = acceleration due to gravity,

→ s = 0 + ½ × 10 × (0.8)² [Intial velocity will be zero]

s = 3.2 m

→ Therefore, the ledge is 3.2 m high from the ground.

questions.question: Raghuvir obtained an average of 25 marks in 12 tests. Rumela has been maintaining an average of 23 marks so far, but she has taken only 8 of the tests. How much does Rumela have to score on an average in the remaining 4 tests to match Raghuvir’s performance?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Raghuvir obtained an average of 25 marks in 12 tests.

Rumela has been maintaining an average of 23 marks so far.

She has taken only 8 of the tests.

**Concept used:**

Total weight = Average weight × Number of boxes

Average = Number of scores/Number of tests

**Calculation:**

Average = Number of scores/Number of tests

Marks scored by Rahuvir in 12 tests = 25 × 12

⇒ 300 

Marks scored by Rumela in first 8 tests = 23 × 8

⇒ 184

Marks required by Rumela in the next 4 tests to match the average of Raghuvir

⇒ 300 – 184

⇒ 116

Required average = Marks required/Number of tests

⇒ 116/4

⇒ 29

**∴ Rumela has to score 29 on an average in the remaining 4 tests to match Raghuvir’s performance.**

questions.question: What day would it be on 29th March 2020?
questions.solution:
As 2000 is divisible by 400 the number of odd days is 0.

Number of leap years till 2019 = 4 (2004, 2008, 2012 and 2016)

Number of ordinary years till 2019 = 15

Number of odd days till 2020 = 15 + (4 × 2) = 23 odd days

Number of odd days in January 2020 = 3

Number of odd days in February 2020 (2020 is the leap year) = 1

Total number of odd days till 29th March 2020 = 23 + 3 + 1 + 29 = 56 odd days = 0 odd days

So, the day on 29th March 2020 is Sunday.

questions.question: Rakesh and Ranjit can complete a task in 4 and 6 days, respectively when working alone. Ranjit started working on the task, and was joined by Rakesh after 2 days. How many days will they require to complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Rakesh and Ranjit can complete a task in 4 and 6 days, respectively when working alone.

Ranjit started working on the task, and was joined by Rakesh after 2 days.

**Formula:**

Work = Time × Efficiency

**Calculation:**

⇒ Work completed by Rakesh in 1 day = 1/4

⇒ Work completed by Ranjit in 1 day = 1/6

⇒ Work completed by Ranjit in 2 days = 2 × (1/6) = 1/3

⇒ Work left = 2/3

⇒ Work completed by Ranjit and Rakesh in 1 day = 1/4 + 1/6 = 5/12

∴ Time taken by Ranjit and Rakesh to complete the remaining work = (2/3)/(5/12) = 1.6 days

**∴ required number of days = 1.6 days**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**

LCM of (4, 6)= 12

efficiency of Rakesh =12 / 4 = 3 units

the efficiency of Ranjit =12 / 6 = 2 units

total efficiency is 5 units per day.

2-day work of Ranjit is = 2 x 2units = 4 units,

remaining work = 12 - 4 = 8 unit

time = work / efficiency.

time= 8/5 = 1.6 days.

Please go through the alternate solution.

Thank you.

• B.R. Ambedkar was also the first Law Minister of India.

questions.question: The size of the image formed by a converging mirror when the object is placed at principal focus is _________.
questions.solution:
• When the object is placed at the principal focus in case of converging or concave mirror then the parallel ray of light pass through the principal focus F giving us the reflected ray.
 
• And the second ray of light passes through the center of curvature C and is reflected along the same path forming another reflected ray. In this case, both the reflected rays will become parallel to each other so these rays cannot intersect each other and the image will be formed at infinity.
 
• The image formed in this case will be highly magnified, real and inverted.

questions.question:
Read the given statement(s) and conclusions carefully and select which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s).

**Statement:**

 
• All wool are yarn.
 
• Some wool are rough.

**Conclusions:**

 
• All rough are wool.
 
• Some Yarn are rough.
questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram of the given statements is as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/379c0c2753cbf3b1518826245aac1c567b4e170d88a8aea65bce77d7ac6210a7.png] 

**Conclusions:**

I. All rough are wool → False (it is possible but not definite)

II. Some Yarn are rough → True.

Hence, “only conclusion II follows”.

questions.question: A galvanometer is used to:

options.text: detect the direction of the sound
detect the direction of the current
detect the direction of magnetic induction

questions.solution:
• The galvanometer is an instrument for measuring value and direction of a small electrical current or a function of the current by deflection of a moving coil.
 
• The deflection is a mechanical rotation derived from forces resulting from the current.
 
• An ammeter is also used for measuring the magnitude of the current.
 
• Galvanometer was invented by Johann Schweigger in 1820.
